text:
ross: Flagging a UX hole in the Go SDK generator: if creds block during refresh, cancelling the parent ctx doesn't always abort the in-flight handshake. Repro below.

ross: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
creds := &slowCreds{sleep: 2 * time.Second}
cli := NewClient(WithCreds(creds))
g, _ := cli.Generator(ctx, "redwood-small")
// cancel soon after starting
go func() { time.Sleep(100*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
// observed: Stream() hangs until creds return
if _, err := g.Stream(ctx); err != nil { log.Printf("err: %v", err) }
```

elaine: Ugh. Customers will hit this in sample apps. Two compatible fixes: add GetToken(ctx) so refresh is cancelable, or add a generator.Abort()/Close() that forcibly tears down handshake.

priya: I prefer both: quick ship Abort() as an escape hatch and follow up with a creds API change for parity with Python/Node. Abort() helps onboarding while we migrate.

harry: If we add Abort(), we must document lifetime guarantees: Abort() should unblock handshake and cause Stream() to return promptly with a cancellable error. Also add a default handshake timeout in client options (5s) to help flaky creds.

ross: Proposal: 1) add Generator.Abort() and make Stream() observe Abort immediately; 2) add ClientOption HandshakeTimeout with sane default; 3) start RFC to require GetToken(ctx) on creds interface and provide a shim that wraps old creds until migration.

elaine: Also add a tiny sample-app note in onboarding that shows both patterns: using context.WithTimeout for the handshake and calling g.Abort() from another goroutine when desired. Example snippet to put in README.

sdk-bot: [ci-bot] Canary detected generator goroutine growth on canary-e2e; created INF-4200.

priya: I'll draft the Abort() API and a minimal compatibility shim. Harry, can you add the onboarding sample and handshakeTimeout config? I'll include a unit test simulating slow creds + cancel and assert no goroutine leak.

harry: Will do. Also add a CHANGELOG note explaining the creds migration and showing migration snippet.

ross: Thanks all. Marking this for SDK parity triage next week.
